name: What size should an in-law suite be for an aging parent?

mainEntity.name: What size should an in-law suite be for an aging parent?
mainEntity.text: What size should an in-law suite be for an aging parent?

acceptedAnswer.text: The right size depends less on square footage and more on how the suite will be used every day. For an aging parent, a compact but efficient layout is often better than a larger unit with wasted space. The suite should allow easy circulation, minimal steps, accessible bathroom clearances, and enough room for mobility aids if needed. Good lighting, easy-to-reach storage, and a simple path from the entrance to the bathroom and bedroom are just as important as the overall size. If care needs may change later, the design should leave room for future modifications. The best approach is to build for comfort, safety, and ease of use first, then expand only if the site and budget support it.
acceptedAnswer.description: For an aging parent, the best in-law suite size is usually the smallest layout that still allows easy movement, a comfortable bathroom, storage, and enough room for a bed and seating area. Accessibility matters more than total square footage. A well-planned compact suite can be better than a larger but awkward one.
